inputs.source: Published HR policy documents, authored by the HR content team, two-person review before publish

instructions.note: 'Do not give legal advice' is the only guard against scope creep into legal advice; nothing structural backs it up.

controls.name: Read-only credential scoped to policy index
controls.decay_rationale: Scoped credential grants read-only access to the policy index only; the agent cannot acquire broader access regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Two-person review required before publishing policy content
controls.decay_rationale: Human publish-review process is enforced outside the model and does not weaken as model capability grows, though it may miss subtle injected instructions hidden in long policy text.

controls.name: Network-layer denial of all outbound egress, pen-test verified
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced at the network layer independent of model behavior; verified by penetration test. Fails if a new tool requires an egress channel that gets allowlisted, or if the rule is disabled without review.

controls.name: Chat client disables image rendering and automatic link fetch
controls.decay_rationale: Client-side rendering restriction prevents classic markdown-image or auto-fetch exfiltration channels regardless of model output.

controls.name: Reply destination bound to the authenticated requester's session
controls.decay_rationale: The recipient of every reply is fixed by the authenticated session from the system of record, not chosen by model output, so the model cannot redirect a reply to an unintended party. Fails only if this binding is disabled without review.

controls.name: Model version pinned; upgrade requires change ticket
controls.decay_rationale: Pinning stops silent upgrades, but an approved change ticket can still raise model capability over time, so dependent controls elsewhere will eventually face a stronger model.

controls.name: System prompt instruction: do not give legal advice
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to follow the instruction; a more capable model or one manipulated via injected text in policy content can rationalize exceptions.

controls.name: Tool definition pinning or hashing for policy_search.search
controls.decay_rationale: Not evidenced in any artifact; recommended to prevent an undetected change to the tool's schema or description.

controls.name: Audit logging of searches and replies
controls.decay_rationale: Not evidenced in any artifact; a detective control here would support repudiation resistance and incident review.

findings.title: Internal policy content read then returned to requester (read-then-send pattern)

attack_path.note: Published, two-person-reviewed policy content lives here, write-restricted to the HR content team.
Content enters the agent's context as search results.
Agent reads the matching policy via a read-only, least-privilege credential.
Agent quotes the policy content back to the authenticated requester; destination is bound to the session, not chosen by the model.

forecast.watch_signal: A new tool or egress channel added to the agent, or a change to the network egress rule or reply-routing configuration made without going through security review.

evidence.observation: Policy index holds published policies, internal sensitivity, write restricted to HR content team with two-person review.
Agent credential is read only and scoped to the policy index.
Replies go only to the authenticated requester's chat session; the chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links.
Agent has no network egress; denial is enforced at the network layer and verified by a pen test.
Agent is instructed to quote the retrieved policy text, so internal content is included verbatim in the reply.

recommendations.action: Add tool definition pinning or hashing for policy_search.search so a later change to its schema or description cannot go unnoticed.
Add audit logging of search queries and reply content, tied to the authenticated employee identity, so a future egress-channel change can be reviewed against a record of normal behavior.

findings.title: Scope creep past 'no legal advice' guard relies on a dependent behavioral control (potential indirect injection via policy text)

attack_path.note: Internally authored policy text, reviewed by two people but not screened for embedded instructions, enters the agent's context.
Agent retrieves and quotes the text verbatim, per prompt.md:2.
Agent could be steered, by an embedded instruction or by a persistent model behavior, to give legal advice or other out-of-scope guidance despite prompt.md:4.

forecast.watch_signal: The model version or provider changes (even via the change-ticket process), or the agent's purpose or typical interaction length grows beyond simple single-turn policy Q&A.

evidence.observation: 'Do not give legal advice' is the only control against scope creep, and it is a prompt instruction with no structural backstop.
The agent is instructed to quote the policy text directly, so any text embedded in a published document, including instruction-like text, enters the model's context verbatim.
Policy documents are written by the HR content team and reviewed by two people before publish, which lowers but does not eliminate the chance of an embedded instruction reaching the model's context.

recommendations.action: Add an output-side check (deterministic pattern match or a separate classifier) that flags or blocks replies containing legal-advice language, instead of relying solely on the system prompt instruction.
Extend the two-person publish review checklist to explicitly screen for embedded instructions or prompt-injection patterns in policy text before publication.

findings.title: No declared audit trail for searches or replies (repudiation gap)

attack_path.note: Search queries are not described as logged.
Replies are not described as logged, so misuse or a bad answer cannot be reconstructed after the fact.

forecast.watch_signal: Any expansion of the agent's data scope or purpose beyond published HR policy Q&A, which would make the absence of an audit trail more consequential.

evidence.observation: No logging, audit trail, or monitoring of searches or replies is described in any artifact.

recommendations.action: Log every search query, matched policy, and reply text with the authenticated employee id and timestamp, retained per HR data policy.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk reaches moderate because internal (I-trust) policy content is read and returned to the requester, and because that same I-trust source could in principle carry an embedded instruction (goal hijack). No untrusted (U) source reaches any capability in this design, which keeps inherent risk well below the ceiling typical of agents that ingest outside content. Residual risk is low: the reply destination is bound to the authenticated session rather than chosen by the model, and all network egress is denied at the network layer and pen-test verified, so the two independent structural controls together sever any path to an attacker-controlled destination (rubric step 1). The one finding with no structural backstop, scope creep past the 'no legal advice' instruction, falls to the low floor only through the behavioral credit at step 4, not through a severing control. Forecast risk rises to moderate because that behavioral instruction is dependent and fails under model_upgrade or longer_task_horizon, and because adding a new egress-capable tool or removing the network-deny/destination-binding controls without review would reopen the internal-data disclosure path before any equivalent control is in place for the new capability.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, tools.json, and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP configuration, IaC, or source code was provided; the network egress denial and credential scoping are taken as declared/verified per the runtime notes without independent verification beyond what is stated.
No logging or audit configuration was provided, so the absence of detective controls is inferred from silence in the artifacts, which may understate controls that exist but were not described.

Protocol-level details (for example, whether policy_search.search runs via MCP or a direct function call) were not provided, so protocol-specific checks such as auth method and peer identity could not be applied.
max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are inferred from the described single-tool, single-turn architecture (search then reply) and are not explicit numeric limits stated in the artifacts.
